findings.problem: The quote is a v5.0.0 docs passage describing how the option works, not a statement that anything changed from 4.x, so it does not support 'changed what taskTitleValueFormatTruncate does'; quote a source that states the loupe.inspect-to-pretty-format change and how it affects title values.

The changelog entry is about replacing loupe.inspect with pretty-format for formatting interpolated values, but the symbol is taskTitleValueFormatTruncate, which the entry never mentions; the symbol should name the formatting change itself (test.each/test.for title interpolation), or the lesson should be dropped.

The sentence says the option's behavior changed but never says how, and its advice to 'increase taskTitleValueFormatTruncate if truncated' applies to both versions, so an assistant learns nothing actionable and misses that every interpolated title is now formatted by pretty-format; state the actual observable difference (e.g. the 4.1.11 truncation of a 50-char value at limit 100 no longer happens) or reframe around the formatter change.
The lesson has no quote, so nothing states the fact itself or names the symbol; add a quote saying `coverage.exclude` no longer inherits negation globs (e.g. `!pattern`) from `test.include`.
The symbol "coverage.exclude test.include" joins two config keys into one name that isn't a real symbol; the changed option is `coverage.exclude`, so use that and mention `test.include` in the claim.

The sentence says vitest changed what `coverage.exclude` does in general, but the tests only show that one negation glob (`!something`) in `test.include` is no longer inherited; narrow the claim to negation-glob inheritance from `test.include`.
The sentence never says what changed: an assistant can't tell that files matched by a `test.include` negation glob are now counted in coverage again; state the before/after behavior explicitly.

The lesson has no tests, so nothing shows that substring-matching code passes on the release before 5.0.0 and fails on 5.0.0 with a mismatch error; add a differential pair that pins the boundary and the symptom.

The claim does not say this is the browser-mode `expect.element(...).toHaveTextContent` assertion, or that it used to match substrings, so an assistant could apply it to jest-dom/@testing-library matchers or miss that partial-text assertions now fail; scope it to vitest browser assertions and state that partial matches should move to `toMatchTextContent`.

The sentence "changed what `vitest.config` does" is vague and suggests the config file's contents or semantics changed, when the actual change is that Vitest no longer searches ancestor directories for a config file; reword it to say that running vitest from a subdirectory no longer picks up a vitest.config/vite.config in a parent directory, and that you should pass --config or --root, or put the config in the project root.

The docs quote only describes the lookup in the project `root` and never says that ancestor directories are no longer searched, so it does not state the change itself; use a quote (for example from the PR #10428 or the v5 migration notes) that explicitly says config files are not looked up from ancestor directories.

The lesson has no quote at all, and the only source text is the headline 'Allow mutating happy-dom/jsdom window object', which never names window.innerWidth; add a quote from the commit or issue that states the fact (assigning a window property like innerWidth now reaches the happy-dom/jsdom window, so matchMedia sees it) and names the symbol.

The sentence is unscoped, but the evidence covers only assigning window.innerWidth under --environment=happy-dom (happy-dom 20.0.0); scope the claim to assignment in the happy-dom environment, or add a jsdom test before claiming jsdom too.

'changed what window.innerWidth does' doesn't say what changed, so an assistant can't tell that before 5.0.0 assigning window.innerWidth only set a global and didn't affect the DOM environment (e.g. matchMedia), while from 5.0.0 it does; state that old-vs-new behavior so the assistant doesn't keep writing workarounds or misread test results.

The sentence "changed what `Temporal` does" suggests the Temporal API itself changed, when the change is that `vi.useFakeTimers()` now fakes `Temporal.Now`/`Temporal` along with Date; the claim should say that Temporal now follows the fake clock under `vi.useFakeTimers()`, so an assistant does not write wrong code around Temporal outside fake timers.

The claim leaves out the scope that the quote and tests depend on: Temporal is faked only when a global `Temporal` exists (native Node >= 26, a flag, or a global polyfill), and the tests only cover a hand-rolled global on Node 24 with `Temporal.Now.instant()`; the claim should state that condition and not imply the whole Temporal API is covered.

The symbol is `Temporal`, a global the project does not own, but the behavior that changed belongs to `vi.useFakeTimers` (the entry says fake-timers "support mocking `Temporal`"); the symbol should be `vi.useFakeTimers`, with Temporal named in the claim.

The lesson has no quote stating the fact: the generated sentence only says vitest 'changed what `test.for/each $` does'. Add a quote that names `test.each`/`test.for` `$` title interpolation and says that string values are no longer wrapped in quotes (e.g. `'alice'` becomes `alice`).
The claim implies `$` interpolation changed in general, but the tests only cover string values in object rows (`$name`, `$who`). Narrow the claim to string values in `$`-interpolated titles.

'Changed what `test.for/each $` does' does not tell an assistant what the new behavior is and could suggest `$` variables no longer work. State the concrete outcome: titles now show `each greets alice`, not `each greets 'alice'`, which matters for `-t` filters, snapshots, and reporters that match titles.

The changelog gives the old default as `.vitest-attachements/` (misspelled), but the test only checks `.vitest-attachments`, so on 4.1.11 the attachment lands in a directory the test never lists and the run prints 'ERROR: attachment not found in either directory' instead of the expected FAIL; the test should check `.vitest-attachements` (and its FAIL message should name that directory).

The lesson has no quote at all, so nothing ties the claim to a stated fact about `coverage.include`. Add a quote that states the actual fix (directory-like include/exclude globs no longer match sibling paths that share the prefix) and names `coverage.include`, rather than relying on the changelog headline "globs too eager".

"Changed what `coverage.include` does" reads as a general change to include semantics, but the tests only show one case: the bare directory pattern 'src' no longer matching the sibling file src-file-in-root.js. Narrow the claim to that case.

The sentence never says what changed, so an assistant cannot tell which configs are affected or how to write them correctly. State the concrete behavior instead: since 5.0.0, a pattern like `include: ['src']` matches only files inside `src/`, and no longer matches prefix-sharing siblings like `src-file-in-root.js`, so those files silently drop out of coverage.

The quote only describes the default cache location and links `fsModuleCachePath`; it never states that `fsModuleCache` is now a top-level option. Replace it with a doc line that says `fsModuleCache` itself is a top-level config option, for example one that names it alongside its former `experimental.fsModuleCache` location.

"Older versions don't have it" will lead an assistant to think module caching is unavailable before 5.0.0, but the test's own Run 1 shows `experimental.fsModuleCache` works on 4.1.11. The claim should say only the top-level placement is new and that older versions use `experimental.fsModuleCache`.

"Older versions don't have it" claims more than the tests show, since the tests only prove the top-level key is ignored on 4.1.11 while the feature exists there under `experimental`. Narrow the claim to the top-level key.

kind "renamed" with symbol experimental_clearCache contradicts the evidence: the 5.0.0 test calls experimental_clearCache successfully, so the old name was not renamed away; this change adds `clearCache` (promoted from experimental), so kind should be "added" and symbol "clearCache", with no replacement.

"renamed `experimental_clearCache` to `clearCache`" leads an assistant to treat the old name as gone or deprecated and to rewrite working code; the sentence should say `clearCache` is now available as a stable method and `experimental_clearCache` still works in 5.0.0.

The quote names only `experimental_clearCache` and says when it appeared (4.0.11), not that `clearCache` exists in 5.0.0; quote the doc line that names `clearCache` as a stable Vitest method, alongside this note.

The lesson has no tests, only documentation quotes, so nothing shows the same code passing on the first release in range and failing on the release before; add a differential test pair, for example one asserting `typeof JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(locator)) === 'object'`.

signal: silent is unsupported: the entry says locators changed from a string to an object, so older code that treats a serialized locator or a command argument as a selector string (string methods, string comparison) can throw or behave differently; signal must be backed by a test showing old-style code runs without error, or be changed.

The claim "Vitest automatically unwraps a Locator" has no scope, but the quote is a fragment about a specific context (passing a locator to custom commands or transports); limit the claim to the context the docs and tests actually cover.

The second quote "vitest will automatically unwrap it to a SerializedLocator" does not say what "it" is, where the unwrapping happens, or name the Locator symbol; quote the full sentence that states the fact.

The changed symbol is Locator (its serialization and toJSON), not SerializedLocator, which is the new return type; also, docs fetched at the v5.0.0 tag do not show that 5.0.0 is the first release with the change, so set symbol to Locator and confirm the start version against the commit 80f07edf6.

The sentence never says that locators used to serialize to a selector string, and its claim that old code "still runs" would lead an assistant to keep code that expects a string; state the old-to-new change and its effect on string-expecting code.

The entry adds a new argument ("`thresholds.autoUpdate` to receive previous threshold as argument"), and code that doesn't use it behaves the same, so kind should be "added", not "behavior". "behavior" makes the sentence say vitest "changed what `autoUpdate` does", but autoUpdate does the same thing and only gets an extra second parameter.

The claim "changed what `concurrent` does" covers every use of `concurrent`, but the tests only show one case: a top-level `test(..., { concurrent: false })` run under global `sequence.concurrent`. Narrow the claim to say that `concurrent: false` on a top-level test now opts it out of the global `sequence.concurrent` setting.

An assistant reading "changed what `concurrent` does" could think `test.concurrent`, `describe.concurrent` or `concurrent: true` now behave differently, which nothing shows. Name the case that changed: `concurrent: false` used to be ignored at top level under `sequence.concurrent` and now makes those tests run one after another.

The quoted docs also cover opting out of `describe.concurrent`, which the tests never run and which the entry doesn't describe as new. Either add a differential test for that case or keep the claim limited to `sequence.concurrent`.

The lesson has no quote, so nothing states the fact or names the symbol; add a quote saying that vitest now applies CJS interop only when `__esModule` is truthy, so a CommonJS dependency with `exports.__esModule = false` is imported like plain CJS with a `default` key holding `module.exports`.

The claim "changed what `__esModule` does" covers every `__esModule` value and every import path, but the tests only check a node_modules CommonJS dependency with `__esModule = false` imported via `import * as ns`; narrow the claim to falsy `__esModule` on CommonJS dependencies, or add tests for other falsy values and import forms.

An assistant reading "changed what `__esModule` does" can't tell which way it changed and could wrongly assume interop for truthy `__esModule` (the common case) changed; the sentence should say that CJS deps with a falsy `__esModule` no longer get ESM interop, so the `import *` namespace now has a `default` key and its enumerable keys differ.
